description: New World review: Arctic snow is centred near 65 degrees north, with a broad 3-degree transition shaped by deterministic geographic variation and calibrated elevation, rather than a straight latitude stripe. Only already-cold tundra/alpine land is eligible; steep exposed ground retains grey rock. Elsewhere, only peaks above an authored high mountain snowline are snowy: 5000 metres at the equator, falling 20 metres per degree of absolute latitude, with a 4000-metre floor. Local relief is normalized to the 500-cell map before the 220-metre exposed-rock cutoff. This is approximate art direction, not measured seasonal snow cover. Water and calibrated elevations are unchanged.
